Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: contact@midwest-safety.com

The suspect identified as 24-year-old Garrett Trammell was transported to an area hospital for evaluation where a search warrant was executed for a blood draw. His blood tested positive for THC, which Trammell's defense attorney argued he had smoked two weeks prior. According to a local news report, data pulled from the black box in Trammell's truck indicated that he never hit the brakes and made a sharp turn in the direction of Officer Wells. Officer Wells was placed on maximum life support and underwent multiple surgeries, including the amputation of part of his left leg. Trammell was transported to jail, where he was charged with assault and battery by means or force. Likely to produce death, four counts of assault and battery with a deadly weapon, endangering others while attempting to elude an officer and leaving the scene of a collision involving injury. The judge set his bond at $950,000, which he posted. According to posts on his Facebook account, Trammel enjoyed fishing trips, concerts, and holidays with his friends and family while out on bond. Nearly two years later, Trammell entered a blind guilty plea where he pleaded guilty without a prior agreement on punishment, leaving sentencing entirely up to the judge's discretion. The judge sentenced him to 25 years and probation for the rest of his life. Trammell is currently incarcerated at Allen Gamble Correctional Center and will have to serve 21 years before he is eligible for parole.
